Porcelain tile is the workhorse here. Density near zero porosity, so water doesn’t soak in, and the glaze resists scratches and stains from toothpaste, soap, hair dye, whatever hits it.

Ceramic tile is fine too, but the body is more porous unless you buy higher PEI ratings. Still cheaper, still durable, just watch the grout lines more.

Vinyl plank composite, if you want softer underfoot and cheaper install, but it can’t take the same steam load as tile. Cheap enough to replace when it goes.

Glass tile looks nice but chips if you drop the toothbrush holder, and the grout lines collect grime. Skip unless you want a spa vibe and have time to clean daily.

As for natural stone, you already ruled it out, good call. Granite’s a step above marble but still needs sealing.

For your scenario—kids, daily blasts of humidity, minimal maintenance—stick with full-body porcelain, 1/8” or thicker, matte or satin finish for slip resistance. Size 12”x24” or bigger reduces grout lines, less places for mold.

Install with polymer-modified thinset, use a sanded epoxy grout, and you’re set for decades without a reseal.

- Rest 15 minutes before carving.

Gluten-free gravy:  
1. Pour off the fat from the roasting pan, skim the drippings, add 1½ cups chicken stock.  
2. Heat on medium, whisk 2 tablespoons cornstarch dissolved in 2 tablespoons cold water until thickened.  
3. Adjust salt and pepper; keep warm.

Sides that fit the lactose constraint and roast alongside the chicken:  
- Roasted carrots: toss 2 pounds carrots in olive oil, salt, pepper; roast on the same sheet 30 minutes, then add to the pan.

- Quick-glazed Brussels sprouts: halve 1 pound sprouts, toss with 2 tablespoons maple syrup, 1 tablespoon olive oil, roast last 20 minutes with the carrots.

If you want a single-pan finish, start the chicken, then add carrots at minute 30, Brussels sprouts at minute 40. Potatoes can be boiled on the stovetop while everything roasts.
